summary: Preinstall drops Bun runtime to execute obfuscated payload unrelated to rollup config
details: The package's package.json declares a preinstall hook (`node setup.mjs`) that runs automatically on `npm install`. setup.mjs is obfuscated (hex-named identifiers, split string maps) and downloads the Bun runtime archive from github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v1.3.13/<platform>.zip, extracts the bun binary, chmods it executable, and invokes it against a sibling file `math_init.js`. `math_init.js` is a 727 KB obfuscated blob consisting of a large opcode/constant array and a string-array rotator function, with no human-readable strings and no relation to the package's stated purpose (a rollup configuration helper). The effect on install is that an alternate language runtime is fetched and used to execute an obfuscated payload the Node ecosystem cannot readily inspect. This is the alternate-runtime dropper pattern: the Bun binary itself comes from Bun's official release host, but Bun is being used solely to execute a bundled obfuscated payload whose behavior is opaque and unrelated to the advertised functionality.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
